Re-check the framing after the cap-width fix below; the current size uses w*0.6, which is inflated by the oversized cap.

issues.problem: The cap is far too wide. ExplosionProfile.head_state grows radius with grow=1-(1-1.25*tanh(t/tau))^1.6, so it reaches ~35% of cap_r (30.5 km) by 40 s. The cap is about 25 km wide at 40 s, ~33 km at 60 s and ~54 km at 90 s. The dossier gives 9 km at 60 s and 61 km at 10 min. The result is a 4:1 pale pancake hovering about 2 km over the ground on a stubby stem: no rising cauliflower ball, no torus, wrong stem-to-cap ratio. Heights are roughly right (about 14 km at 60 s, 18 km at 90 s); only the width is wrong.
issues.fix: Decouple cap radius from the rise. Add per-bomb keyframes read in head_state, interpolated in log time: cap_d_keys=[[30,7000],[60,9000],[156,20000],[342,40000],[600,61000],[1800,100000]] and optionally top_keys=[[60,13000],[90,17000],[156,31000],[210,33000],[342,36000],[600,37000]]. Interim: r = max(start_r, cap_r*clamp(t/(0.95*t_stab),0,1)), which spreads roughly linearly in time. Keep half-thickness at about 0.4*r while r < 10 km so the 40-90 s head is a tall boiling ball.

issues.problem: The fireball is a uniformly clipped pure-white disc with a soft grey halo from 0.1 s to 20 s. The high-speed reference shows a mottled, patchy surface; the dossier calls for 'sun half-risen' white to yellow-white, then yellow-orange to orange-red with dark veins at 5-15 s. None of that colour progression or surface detail survives. The model is also too hot late: BlastPhysics.fireball_temperature gives about 4700 K at 10 s and 3400 K at 20 s for 10.4 Mt.
issues.fix: (a) Exposure, in explosion.gd metered_luminance: spot-meter the ball when it fills the binocular view. Raise the cov weight (pow(ang_r/half_fov,2)*6 -> *12) and meter to about 0.3*l_fb, so the ball sits about +1.5 EV, not +3-4 EV. AgX with agx_white 16 bleaches everything above ~4 to white. (b) Late cooling, in ExplosionProfile.fireball_state: add art key cool_k (Mike ~0.6), temp *= lerp(1, cool_k, smoothstep(2*t2, 8*t2, t)), aiming at ~4000 K at 5 s, ~2500 K at 12 s and <2000 K by 20 s. (c) Start the dark 'skin' at t/t2 = 2 instead of 8 (fireball_state skin).

issues.problem: A huge opaque, matte dark-grey smooth hemisphere (~13 km wide) sits over the fireball from 10 s to ~34 s like a smoked-glass bowl. It is the WilsonLayer: t0 = (W/20)^(1/3) = 8 s, visible to t0 + 2.2*1.5*t0. The dossier wants a brilliant white, translucent Wilson cloud that flashes at 1-5 s only.
issues.fix: fx_layers.gd now zeroes Wilson above 150 kt, so re-render to confirm the dome is gone. For Mike, set wilson_force=True, wilson_start=1.0 and wilson_duration=0.3 (about 1-5 s). In wilson.gdshader, light the veil by the fireball (replace col += g_fireball_color*w*0.02 with about 0.5*g_fireball_color.rgb*w*(R_fb/d)^2) and lower the opacity floor (0.18 -> 0.08) so it reads as a bright translucent veil, not a grey bowl.

issues.problem: The stem is a clean pale blue-white cylinder, the same tone as the haze. The reference colour photo shows a dark red-brown dirty stem under a white cap, and the dossier gives a wide dirty grey-brown stem 3-4 km across. The stem/cap colour contrast, which is Mike's main read, is gone.
issues.fix: Darken stem_color [0.50,0.45,0.40] to about [0.30,0.22,0.16]. In explosion_volume.gdshader, scale the aerial-perspective blend for the volume (mix(acc, fog.rgb*alpha, fog.a*0.45)); at 90 km fog.a currently washes every albedo to sky-blue. Add a warm glow to the upper stem for the first ~90 s.

issues.problem: rings=3 render as thick CG 'life-saver' tori. sdf_rings uses a radial factor of 0.35 and thickness 0.12*rr, giving bands about 1.7 km thick and 6 km wide with a sky-coloured hole between stem and ring. The lower ring has a specular-looking hot spot at its left end. Mike needs smooth, thin, laminar pileus sheets cutting across the stem at 2.5-6 min.
issues.fix: Replace the torus in sdf_rings with a flat disc: max(abs(p.y-y0)-th, r-rr), th 150-300 m, rr 2-3x the stem radius, no inner hole. Apply noise only on the outer edge, amplitude <=0.05*rr, at low frequency. Time them t_on ~150 s, life ~200 s (new ring_t_on/ring_life art keys). Use a gentler phase for rings (mix(1,phase,0.3)).

issues.problem: A surface burst renders as a sphere floating about 1.2 km above the ground at 2-20 ms; a 150 m ball is hanging in mid-air. The cause is in fireball_state: center_y = rise*0.92 with rise = head_center_y(t) - hob, and head_center_y(0) = r_fb_max*0.5 for surface bursts. The reference shows a flat-based hemisphere sitting on the sea.
issues.fix: In fireball_state, use rise = head_center_y(t) - head_center_y(0). Keep center_y = 0 (hemisphere on the ground) until lift-off at ~10 s ('hover 5-15 s then lift'), then ease up with smoothstep. Note that at 90 km the first ~30 ms should sit below the horizon, about 380 m of curvature drop.

issues.problem: The required water curtain at the base is missing. The skirt is a flat white slab 300-600 m high with vertical outer walls, which reads as a white cake.
issues.fix: For Mike, in skirt_state set st['inner'] to about 0.7 and add art keys curtain_h ~1500 m and curtain_t, so a ring wall rises by 20-30 s and collapses by 90 s. In sdf_skirt, drop the vertical sheet edge (keep only the rolling torus front with a thinning tail) so the front is rounded and ragged.

issues.problem: The ice cap reads as a fluffy cotton 'hat brim' around the cap at mid-height. ice_state places y = top + 0.1*half - 0.25*r with r = 1.1*R_head, so on the over-wide head the shell equator wraps the side. It is also cumulus-noisy rather than a silky veil.
issues.fix: In ice_state, cap r at 1.05*R_head and only allow it while the head is <15 km wide (20-120 s). In the shell branch of the shader, use low-frequency noise with amplitude <=0.05*z and a sharper outer edge, so it is a smooth sunlit veil.

issues.problem: The cap is a blurry low-detail blob. head_density sets the noise cell to max(R,H)*0.55, so on a 30-50 km cap the finest billows are about 5 km across. The edge softness H*0.03 smears ~1 km, giving an out-of-focus cotton look with weak self-shadowing. The reference shows crisp cauliflower turrets.
issues.fix: Base the cell size on H (cell = H*head_noise_scale, with head_noise_scale ~0.25), add a 4th billow octave, set billow_sharp 0.6 -> 1.3 and edge = min(H*0.01, 150 m). Strengthen micro self-shadow (od_local*0.6 -> *1.2, mix 0.65 -> 0.85) and cut ambient (amb*ao*0.6 -> 0.35).

issues.problem: Two signature details are missing: the five lightning channels rising from the sea about 1 km from ground zero, and the low trade-cumulus deck lit orange by the fireball (the main IvyMike2 look). The stem at 360 s also shows horizontal stacked banding.
issues.fix: Add 4-6 short-lived emissive jagged line meshes at about 1 km radius for 5-80 ms. Enable a scattered low cloud layer at 0.6-2 km for Pacific shots. Fix the banding with the raymarch-step item in the systemic list.

issues.problem: The Bravo signature is absent at its key moment. At 40 s, where the references show a glowing boiling fireball cut by several thin stacked condensation discs, there is only a pale 43 km pancake. rings_state switches rings on at t_stab*(0.05+0.025i) = 32/49/65/81 s with life 0.18*t_stab = 117 s, so ring 0 has opacity about 0.13 at 40 s and the rings stay to ~5 min. They show up at 180 s as thick donut tori with holes.
issues.fix: Add art keys to rings_state: ring_t_on=[15,18,22,60], ring_life=[40,40,45,90], ring_y=[3500,5000,8500,9700] (ring 4 dragged from 9 to 16 km over 60-150 s), ring_r=[5000,6000,7000,7000], half-thickness 120-200 m. Draw them as flat lens discs (no hole, sharp laminar top and bottom, albedo ~0.97, brightly lit by the fireball) so they read edge-on as glowing blades like in bravo_condensation_rings_red_sky.jpg.

issues.problem: The cap is 43 km wide at 40 s and about 61 km at 90 s (head_state grow on cap_r = 56.5 km). The dossier gives 11.6 km at 60 s and 24 km at 120 s. Because of this, zoom framing hits the 58 deg clamp and from 90 s shows the bunker window frame, consoles and ceiling, with the cap cut by the window top.

There is no crimson sky. The crimson term (inten = crim*6*exp(-t/25)) only tints a halo around the ball and the 0.02 s sky mauve. By the time exposure recovers (90 s+) it has decayed to ~3%. In noon daylight it is also physically implausible; the references are pre-dawn, with the fireball dyeing the sky and cumulus red-orange for minutes.
issues.fix: Render and ship Bravo at its dossier time of day (pre-dawn, sun -8 deg). In explosion.gd _update_globals, change the crimson decay from exp(-t/25) to exp(-t/150). In sky.gdshader, tint the g_flash scatter term with g_fireball_color.rgb instead of the fixed bluish (0.9,0.93,1.0). Add a low cumulus deck lit by g_fireball_color.

issues.problem: The fireball is a featureless white disc up to 20 s and then disappears inside the pancake by 40 s. The references show a yellow-white core with an orange boiling cauliflower top still very bright at 30-60 s, rising out of the 'clinging' hemisphere.
issues.fix: Let the head grow from the fireball: start_r equal to the fireball radius, density ramping from 15 s to 40 s while fireball opacity fades into the head heat glow. Use core_glow ~1.5 and core_cool so the glow stays orange until ~90 s and turns dull red by 150 s. Apply the exposure and AgX fix from the systemic list.

issues.problem: An opaque grey Wilson hemisphere (wilson=0.8) hides the fireball from 9 s to 39 s. The dossier mentions pileus caps forming over the dome, not a Wilson shell.
issues.fix: Set wilson=0 (and re-render with the new >150 kt rule). Use ice_cap with t_on ~0.008 (about 5 s) as a smooth white pileus draped over the hemisphere, lit by the fireball.

issues.problem: The hemisphere should 'cling to the earth' up to 8-10 s and then spring up. Instead the render shows a sphere floating ~1.6 km above ground from t=0, identical to Mike.
issues.fix: Apply the same fireball_state surface fix as Mike, with lift-off at about 10 s, and squash it to a flat-based dome.

issues.problem: The 'dark 7 km stem' renders pale blue-white because the dark stem_color [0.30,0.25,0.21] is washed out by aerial fog. At 360 s the stem shows a stacked 'screw-thread' pagoda pattern, which is raymarch slicing in a ~100 km proxy box.
issues.fix: Reduce the fog blend on the volume, as for Mike. For the slicing, march only the stem's own cylinder interval, or clamp dt to ~0.05*stem radius when the sample is within 2 stem radii; see the systemic raymarch item.

issues.problem: tier2 (radius_m 30000) renders as translucent glassy diagonal 'cone' smears at the cap edges, because sdf_shell is a hollow shell 7% of z thick. The 2 cone skirts and 3 bells around the stem from the dossier read as glass.
issues.fix: Render tier2 and the bells as solid, smooth, bell-shaped skirts: ellipsoid density with a laminar top and a soft lower edge, not a thin hollow shell. Place them around the stem at 5.5-8 km, growing 7 -> 15 km wide over 1.6-4.2 min.

issues.problem: A small orange glowing speck sits in the middle of the cap underside at 180 s. It is the fireball remnant: the temperature model still gives ~1700 K and opacity ~0.5 at 3 min.
issues.fix: Fade fireball opacity over (t_fb_max .. 3*t_fb_max) regardless of temperature, and use the cool_k late-cooling factor.

issues.problem: Hairline arcs from the shock-shell rim cross the cap and the sky at 40 s and 90 s, reading as a CG glass circle.
issues.fix: In ShockLayer.update, fade strength once p < ~1 psi or once slant > 3*r_fb (or draw the shell behind the volume).

issues.problem: The smoke-rocket trails beside the stem, a nice documentary signature, are missing.
issues.fix: Add 6-10 thin, slightly curved smoke trails launched at t ~ -2 s next to ground zero, as cheap ribbon meshes.

issues.problem: The 40 s frame reads as a cartoon face. A hard-edged white fireball disc is pasted in front of a pale 28 km pancake, with two blurry peach glow lobes left and right (the head-heat glow placed on the torus ring at a = 0.62R) and a white stump below. The fireball and the cloud are two disconnected primitives. The dossier calls for an orange-red fireball rolling into a toroid with a thin pale stem.
issues.fix: Merge the primitives. The head should start at the fireball's radius and centre (start_r = r_fb), with a cap diameter of about 13-16 km at 40-60 s (cap_d_keys). As head density rises, fade fireball opacity into head_heat, so the glow lives in the torus and its crevices, not as a separate sphere.

issues.problem: An opaque dark-grey Wilson dome reaching the ground surrounds the airburst (wilson=0.5). The dossier says a Wilson shell is unlikely in dry air at -20 to -30 C.
issues.fix: Set wilson=0, and re-render to confirm that the new w_kt>150 rule in fx_layers.gd removes it.

issues.problem: The bunker ceiling hides the upper cap at 180 s and 360 s; only the stem and the cap underside are visible. The two-tier ~72/55 km cap that defines the late phase is never on screen.
issues.fix: Apply the systemic zoom-framing fix (hide the bunker layer in binocular view, free pitch to ~30 deg for a 53 km top at 120 km).

issues.problem: There is no visible thermal minimum: the 0.5 s frame is a white ball with an orange halo. The dossier calls for a dull orange-red ball with a dark core at ~0.4 s. BlastPhysics.t_min = 0.0035*W^0.4 gives 0.20 s, and t_second_max gives 3.5 s; the megaton scaling 0.0025*W^0.5 = 0.39 s and 0.032*W^0.5 = 5.0 s match the dossier.
issues.fix: Add art overrides t_min_s=0.4 and t2_s=4.5 in ExplosionProfile._derive (or switch above 1 Mt to the W^0.5 forms). Make sure exposure has not already stopped down so far that the dip is invisible; the dip should read as a visible dim orange ball.

issues.problem: There is no reflected-shock flattening. The ball stays perfectly round. In the Bighorn reference the fireball has a flat, orange-lit underside, and the dossier says the bottom is flattened at 5-6 s with no ground contact.
issues.fix: In sdf_fireball and fireball_density, clip the bottom with a plane y_cut = (hob - R) + k*(t - t_reflect) once t > t_reflect (219: ~5 s, Tsar: ~6-7 s), with ragged noise on the cut. Add art keys flatten_t and flatten_rise_mps, and give the cut face a hotter orange rim.

issues.problem: The colour stays white through 40 s. The dossier progression is white -> yellow (~10 s) -> yellow-orange (~20 s) -> orange-red (~45 s), with the glow gone by 50-90 s.
issues.fix: Apply the cool_k late-cooling factor (about 0.65) and the exposure spot-metering fix. Check the result against these targets: ~4500 K at 10 s, ~3200 K at 20 s, ~2000 K at 45 s.

issues.problem: The rise is too slow. head_center_y with tanh(t/227 s) puts the fireball top at about 13 km at 40 s; the dossier gives 25 km at 40 s.
issues.fix: Use top_keys=[[15,9000],[40,25000],[90,35000],[300,50000],[540,53000]], or an accelerating early phase: f = tanh(t/tau)*(1-exp(-(t/25)^2)) with tau ~90 s.

issues.problem: The ground skirt is a 1-2 km tall flat white 'cake' with vertical walls. The profile is flagged dusty because hob 3750 < 1.3*55*W^0.4 = 4054 m, which forces hk=1. For a 3.75 km airburst over snow, the dossier describes a low, fast snow-dust ring.
issues.fix: Force dusty=false for NUCLEAR_HIGH_AIR, or set skirt=0.25 and skirt_height=0.25, and fade density after ~120 s. Remove the vertical sheet edge in sdf_skirt.

issues.problem: The stem is wrong. At 40 s it is a white rectangular stump with a flat cut top (max(d,dv) in sdf_stem). Later it is a thick white column with a sharp helical sun terminator, like a twisted rope, at 180-360 s. There are also donut rings (rings=2) that dry polar air does not support. The dossier calls for a thin pale stem.
issues.fix: Set rings=0. Soften the stem top with a density ramp over the top 30% plus noise displacement. Use wrap lighting for the stem (macro = dot*0.35+0.65) with noise on the terminator. Reduce stem radius by about 0.6x (stem_radius_m ~1500).

issues.problem: Shape, colour, rings, brim and skirt are a near-copy of Tsar's, and the noon lighting removes the polar-night signature: the unlit dark grey-blue silhouette against twilight and stars after 90 s.
issues.fix: Use tod night/twilight (sun -11.5 deg) as the default for this bomb. After the glow fades, cut the sun term so the cloud becomes a silhouette.

issues.problem: The shape is wrong. fireball_squash=1.15 makes a tall egg with a round bottom. The real Tsar fireball (tsar_fireball_1961.jpg) is a dome with a flat-cut bottom from the reflected shock at 6-8 s, wider than tall.
issues.fix: Set fireball_squash to 0.95-1.0. Implement the bottom-cut plane described under Test 219 (t_reflect ~6.5 s), so the ball looks pushed up from below and never touches the ground.

issues.problem: The colour is pure clipped white with a grey halo from 0.1 s to 40 s. The reference shows a yellow-white dome with an orange rim wrapped in orange-brown glow. The dossier expects a red-orange toroidal dome at 40 s, fading to dull red over 40-70 s.
issues.fix: Apply exposure spot-metering and cool_k (~0.6), targeting ~3500 K at 15 s, ~2400 K at 40 s and <1300 K by 70 s. Raise the glow wrap with a warm fireball_color halo instead of grey bloom.

issues.problem: An opaque dark-grey Wilson bell jar (wilson=0.4) surrounds the ball. At 40 s ring 0 (t_on = 0.05*733 = 37 s, y ~10.8 km) also cuts straight through the white fireball like Saturn's ring, with a white stump of stem below. It looks like a lamp in a glass dome.
issues.fix: Set wilson=0 and rings=0; Tsar's signatures are the two-tier cap and the shock in the sky, not rings. Re-render after the >150 kt Wilson rule.

issues.problem: The two-tier 95/70 km cap is never visible. The bunker ceiling occludes it at 180 s and 360 s, and tier2 only starts at 0.15*t_stab = 110 s and has grown to ~25 km radius by 360 s. tier2 is also a hollow 7%-thick shell, which reads as glass where visible.
issues.fix: Apply the zoom-framing fix. Make tier2 a solid flattened lens: upper ~95 km wide at ~41-45 km, lower main head ~70 km (set cap_radius_m 35000 and tier2 radius_m 47500). Time it to be clearly two-tiered by 6-8 min, and include a 10-min shot in the rig.

issues.problem: Rise and proportions are wrong. The top is about 16-18 km at 40 s against ~30 km in the dossier. At 90 s the cloud is a 35+ km wide pancake only ~25 km tall with a peach glow band through the middle. The dossier gives 40-45 km tall with a ~40 km cap at 1-3 min, white-pink on the sunlit side and blue-grey on the shadow side.
issues.fix: Use top_keys=[[18,10500],[40,30000],[120,42000],[480,67000],[700,64000]] and cap_d_keys=[[50,18000],[150,40000],[600,95000]]. Remove the uniform heat band after ~70 s (core_cool so the glow is gone by 70-80 s).

issues.problem: There are artifacts on the fireball. Dark charred 'burnt-paper' blotches eat the lower limb (patch-noise temperature mix(0.82,1.12,fpatch) gives about 0.3x emission at the edge). A thin hairline circle (the shock-shell rim drawn over the volume) shows inside the disc at 0.5-1 s.
issues.fix: Near the limb (lq>0.85), narrow the patch range to mix(0.95,1.05) and use lower-frequency patches. In ShockLayer, hide the shell while slant < 1.3*fireball radius.

issues.problem: No dull orange-red ball at the thermal minimum. The dossier gives ~0.55 s; the code's t_min is 0.27 s and t2 is 4.9 s, against 0.56 s and 5-7 s in the dossier.
issues.fix: Set t_min_s=0.56 and t2_s=6.0 overrides (or the W^0.5 scaling).

issues.problem: At 40 s the stem is a white rectangular block with a flat top hanging from the ground. At 180 s an orange glowing speck (fireball remnant, still ~1700 K with opacity ~0.5) sits in the cap underside.
issues.fix: Soften the stem top (density ramp plus noise). Fade fireball opacity over t_fb_max..3*t_fb_max independent of temperature.

issues.problem: There is no 'flash to the horizon': at 2-20 ms the sky and snow look like an ordinary hazy day with a small sun. env_ctl.white_out only drives a UI overlay that is not in the captured frames.
issues.fix: Make the flash an in-world effect captured in movie mode: g_flash brightening the whole sky and snow, plus bloom, for the first 0.1-0.3 s.

issues.problem: The Tsar look is lost: low arctic sun (2.3 deg, golden), an overcast deck with the fireball punching a widening hole, and the shock visible in the sky (currently only hairline arcs). Breakaway size is about 3 km at 0.5 s against 4.6-5.5 km in the dossier.
issues.fix: Use a low-sun time of day and an overcast layer below 4 km with a hole growing at the shock radius. Render a visible shock band (condensation flash on the cloud deck). Raise fireball_scale early, or blend toward fireball_r_m sooner.

systemic: The volume is over-lit relative to the terrain. Earth-tone albedos of 0.3-0.48 (DUST, skirt, column) render near-white cream, brighter than the tan ground they came from, so dust reads as snow, cotton, steam or sea foam in every ground burst. Suspect a missing 1/pi factor or a g_sun_light vs DirectionalLight energy mismatch in explosion_volume.gdshader 'light = sun_c*sunlit + amb*ao*0.6'. Calibrate by rendering a skirt with albedo = ground_col: it must match terrain brightness. Drop the 0.65 hack on c_skirt after calibration.

Raymarch banding: the SDF skip `t += max(sd - margin*0.9, dt)` lands every ray at the same distance from the surface, which erases the hash12 dither. The result is stacked-coin stems, terraced caps, horizontal smear lines and contour ripples. It gets worse when the proxy box inflates (skirt height += t*0.8 is unbounded; surge and dust radius). Re-snap to a jittered grid after each skip, clamp dt to about 0.25x the smallest active feature, and keep the box tight.

Hard seams wherever the head meets the stem or column: macro shading and od_far branch on `dh > ds` (kh vs ks), and head_col and stem_col differ. Use density-weighted blending and an smin union of head and stem. Soften the cheap_density clamp (/(H*0.10) is far too sharp and casts black knife-edge shadows).

Nothing evolves after about 10-25 s. rise_norm is a tanh that stabilizes, head noise has no age advection and there is no wind drift, so 15/30/60 s frames are near-identical stills (Tallboy and Grand Slam are pixel-identical in silhouette). For video this reads as a paused image. Add age-based noise advection, wind shear and drift, continued slow rise and dissipation.

Conventional fireball physics is too short and too hot: conventional_fireball_duration = 0.04*W^(1/3) and t_peak 4200-5200 K give a white flash that is grey smoke by 0.15 s. The references show yellow-orange balls with black soot lasting 0.25-0.4 s and flame to 0.6-1.0 s. Add an fb_duration_s override and use about 3000-3300 K peaks.

The Wilson layer is applied to HE bombs and drawn as a milky glass hemisphere (cull_disabled double faces, interior noise, default humidity 0.55 on a desert range). Restrict it to kt-class nuclear bursts in humid presets; the desert default should be dry.

The debris layer uses emissive cubes with a 2.5 s glow decay and uniform sizes, so every ground burst gets a star-field or glitter look. Use dark clods, incandescence of 0.05 s at most, a wide size distribution, dust trails, and ground-impact puffs for fragment fans.

The sdf_skirt 'sheet' has a flat top and a hard vertical outer wall, so all ground bursts get a 'cake' skirt. It also appears at t about 0 and is lit by the fireball scatter term, giving a white rectangle under the flash. DustWallLayer is a dense, light-coloured surf curtain. Both need soft radial falloff, darker ground-matched colour, lower height and fade-out.

Shape grammar is shared: Mk 82 and Mk 84 are scaled copies of one nuclear mushroom, and Tallboy and Grand Slam are scaled copies of one vase. This violates section 6.3. The 'zoom' auto-framing (shot_rig _setup_view_dynamic frames on the head only) also removes absolute scale, so a fixed per-bomb FOV in the video would help show the size progression. For column kinds the framing should use max(column top, surge radius) to avoid the t5->t8 framing jump.

Terrain in the zoom view: full-width bright horizontal stripes and bands (LOD or clipmap seams, or roads at a grazing angle), horizontally smeared ground texture (needs anisotropic filtering or more detail), and a hard tonal seam near the bottom of the frame. In 60 s frames a black bar from the bunker aperture enters the top of the frame. After exposure recovery the sky turns teal-cyan, not a pale desert blue. All of these cheapen every shot.

Craters (the 7 m Mk 82, 13 m Mk 84, 30 m Tallboy, 38 m Grand Slam) are never visible in the zoom renders at the recommended distance. Add a low or near director shot to the review and verify the crater size, lip and ejecta apron.

The raymarch sampling causes banding across all four bombs. In explosion_volume.gdshader the empty-space skip `t += max(sd - margin*0.9, dt)` puts every ray on the same SDF iso-distance, which throws away the per-pixel dither. dt = seg/steps is also set by the whole proxy box, so a skirt hundreds of metres wide forces 20-40 m steps against 30-120 m stems and caps. Together these produce concentric horizontal 'spun-sugar' striations on caps, stacked horizontal slices in stems, and horizontally brushed hairy edges. Fix: re-apply jitter after every skip, e.g. t = t_enter + (ceil((t - t_enter)/dt) + dither)*dt, using blue-noise or IGN dither that varies per frame in movie mode. Clamp the step locally inside each component (min(dt, 0.08*stem_r) in the stem, min(dt, 0.04*head_half) in the head). Raise base_steps for zoom renders.

Volumes are lit too brightly relative to the terrain. Dust skirts render lighter and more neutral than the sunlit desert they were raised from (skirt ~205,200,195 against ground 182,173,159). 'Soot' albedos of 0.06-0.32 render as mid or light grey, so no bomb can show black smoke. Fix: match the volume sun term to the terrain's Lambert response (scale sun_c*sunlit by about 1/π or about 0.5), and scale the 0.05 multiple-scattering floor and amb*ao*0.6 by albedo so dark media stay dark. Make the dust_wall.gdshader lighting (lit*0.9 + amb*0.8) consistent with the same normalization.

The Wilson shell looks like a grey frosted-glass dome. wilson.gdshader is cull_disabled with a base alpha of 0.18, so front and back faces fill the disc with grey mottling. It also shows up where it physically should not (desert sites, a thermobaric bomb, sub-kt surface bursts). Fix: render front faces only, use a limb-only alpha of about pow(1-facing,3), make it bright white with forward scattering, keep it short (≤0.3-0.6 s), and gate it by site humidity (desert presets -> 0).

Exposure behaves wrongly in the zoom view. The cov branch of metered_luminance stops down to the fireball's surface luminance (max_comp up to 11), which turns the noon sky black for seconds even for 11-44 t conventional blasts. A recovery tau of 4.5 s then keeps it dusk-like for 15-20 s. The flash white-out phase (t < ~0.15 s) is missing: the first frames are already darkened. Fix: no cov boost for conventional bursts, cov boost for nuclear bursts only at t < ~3*t2, recovery tau scaled by yield (about 1 s for sub-kt), and an explicit full-frame white-out for the first 0.1-0.15 s of nuclear bursts.

The cloud's internal glow lasts too long for small yields. head_state's core cooling is a fraction of t_stab (core_cool 0.14*t_stab), so sub-kiloton clouds (Davy Crockett, B61) glow orange for 20-30 s. Use an absolute cooling time instead, e.g. core_cool_s of about 1.2*W_kt^0.35 s.

The skirt grows without limit and has a puck-like shape. skirt_state adds +t*0.8 m of height and +2 m/s of radius forever, so skirts balloon into large puffy banks at 180-360 s. sdf_skirt is a uniform slab with rounded vertical ends (a 'hockey puck'), and the colour reads white. Fix: saturate the growth terms, taper the height toward the front, add ragged plumes, fade to 0 by about 1.5-2*t_stab, and use tan colours.

Stem tops are hard-edged and lag the head. sdf_stem's top is a hard max(d, dv) clip, and stem_state's top lags the rising head (speed_rel 0.75-0.8 with stem_delay), which produces flat-topped pipes and caps floating free with a gap. Fade stem density over the top ~2 radii. When a stem should connect, attach it to the head bottom once it forms. Add an explicit detached option for the bombs where the dust column must not join (B61, the Wasp-style shots).

Lack of distinctiveness: Davy Crockett and B61 end as the same symmetric white mushroom with the same cap:stem proportions, and all four bombs share the same white skirt puck. Every cloud is also perfectly axisymmetric and vertical for 6 minutes. Add per-bomb wind drift and shear with height (Little Feller leaned and drifted NNW at about 7 m/s), a narrow-column variant for Davy Crockett, and a detached compact red-brown ball for B61.

Conventional and thermobaric fireballs are handled by one generic hard-coded path. _conventional_fireball ignores fireball_squash and lift, its duration is 0.04*m^(1/3) (far too short for MOAB's 2.5 s of flame), its colour temperatures (5200 K aluminized, 2600 K thermobaric) give either clipped white or a dull mid-tone peach, and the smoke head detaches from the flame. Add per-bomb keys fb_duration_s, fb_temp_peak, fireball_squash, fireball_lift and soot_start, and keep head and flame as one body while the flame burns.

The environment undermines realism and scale in every zoom frame. The horizon is perfectly flat and empty, with no ridgelines (all the Nevada references have mountains behind), and parallel horizontal light stripes run across the whole playa (terrain texture banding at a grazing angle). Nothing in frame gives scale. Add a distant ridge silhouette, break up the stripe artifact, and place a few range objects or vegetation near ground zero.
Framing: in late zoom frames the auto-frame tilt lets the bunker slit edge appear as a black bar at the top of the image (Davy Crockett at 180 and 360 s).

EXPOSURE (worst systemic issue): Explosion.metered_luminance raises env_ctl.max_comp up to 11 stops (spec: 3-8), and step_adaptation recovers with tau 4.5 s while still metering the cooling fireball. Every noon nuke therefore has a pitch-black sky from 0.1 s to 5 s and a dark teal sky until about 20 s, and all sunlit dust and condensation turns charcoal. Fix: cap at 5-6 stops for the bunker/zoom eye, gate fireball metering on temp > 3000 K, and use a recovery tau of about 2 s after the second pulse.

FIREBALL LOOK: from 2 ms to about 1 s every fireball is a clipped white disc inside a huge soft lightbulb glow. It has no limb, no rapatronic mottling, no visible thermal-minimum dip, and white firefly speckles at the edge. After about 2 s it turns into a uniform peach cotton ball. Fix: restrain the glow/bloom (higher HDR threshold, smaller radius), keep the ball 1-2 stops above exposure so its texture reads, soften fireball_density edges, clamp per-sample emission, and remove the hard 'dens<0.04 -> 0' cut in head_density.

CAP INCANDESCENCE: head_heat glow uses core_radius lerp 1.1 -> 0.5 (it covers the whole head) and lasts until 0.14*t_stab (about 45 s for 15-21 kt), with core_glow 1.2-1.4. Every kiloton cap becomes a self-lit salmon-pink ball with no sun or shadow side and no glowing toroid ring. Fix: core_radius about 0.22-0.3, core_cool about 0.04-0.09, core_glow at most about 0.7, and attenuate the glow by optical depth so it only peeks through gaps.

SHAPE LANGUAGE IS IDENTICAL for Grable, Little Boy and Trinity: an egg-shaped cap, a blue-grey streaked stem and a white puck. The causes are generic: (1) the fireball centre rises at 0.92 x the head rise, so two stacked spheres union into an egg; (2) the torus only reaches full at 0.13*t_stab (about 40 s); (3) cap_half = 0.2*cloud_top makes caps taller than wide during the rise; (4) billow noise gives low-contrast cotton, not deep-shadowed cauliflower. Differentiate per bomb (torus timing, cap aspect, colour, wind shear) and raise head_noise_amp and billow_sharp.

LIGHTING TOO FLAT AND PASTEL: the macro term clamp(dot*0.55+0.45)^2, ambient amb*ao*0.6, sunlit*1.1*phase and aerial fog combine so that profile albedos (dark brown stems, rust NOx heads, tan dust) render white, pink or blue-grey. Cap undersides are not darker, stems are not shadowed by the cap, and there is no strong terminator. Calibrate so an albedo-0.2 surface in full sun reads mid-grey at base exposure. Cut ambient on volumes by about 50%, steepen macro (for example smoothstep(-0.2, 0.8, dot(n,L))), double od_far, and make the haze colour warmer and lighter near the ground.

STEMS everywhere have vertical waterfall/curtain streaks (stem_stretch 1.6 plus the age*rise scroll), are translucent at the edges and at the head junction (a glassy blue-grey band), and have flat-cut 'crown' tops before they reach the cap (dv cut in sdf_stem). Use stretch 1.0 with a domain warp and twist, a density fade or cone at the top, higher extinction, and darker albedo.

GROUND DUST: the volume skirt is a symmetric white marshmallow puck with vertical walls and a flat top that stays unchanged for minutes. The DustWall is an open cylinder with constant alpha, so its silhouette produces hard vertical edges at the frame sides, and dust_col about 0.66 lit by sun*0.9 + ambient*0.8 renders near white. Add a grazing-angle alpha fade, azimuthal height noise, darker desert albedo, and dissipation and drift from about t_hit+40 s.

MESH SHELLS LOOK CG: the Wilson and shock SphereMesh shells show hard limbs, latitude-band faceting (Little Boy 2 s, Baker 1.2-2 s) and thin pen-line circles from the refraction rim (Little Boy 0.5 s, Baker 0.2-2 s). Under stopped-down exposure the Wilson shell becomes a dark glass ball. Move condensation into the volume raymarch (sdf_shell with a noisy soft edge), compute any remaining limb terms from analytic normals, and turn the shock into a soft refraction band.

LATE-PHASE FRAMING: the zoom auto-framing in shot_rig._setup_view_dynamic aims at top*0.45 from the bunker eye. From about 40-90 s onward the bunker roof beam and slit frame cut off or hide the cap for every bomb (at 180 s and 360 s only the stem shows). Ice caps, three-layer clouds and rain-out can never be seen. Fix: put the zoom camera at the slit's outer face, or use a director angle when the required pitch exceeds the slit's upper edge, or let the binocular look out from above the slit.

RAYMARCH ARTEFACTS: dt = seg/steps over a proxy box stretched by a multi-km skirt or surge causes slicing and horizontal banding (Baker 240 s cap, Grable 2 s ball top). Screen-space rectangular brightness seams appear in the dust (Grable 2 s and 5 s, a vertical step at frame centre), probably from the soft-particle depth fade reading bunker glass or frame depth. Use per-component march intervals, a dt clamp near the head, and exclude the bunker from the fade depth.

NO WIND: every cloud stays perfectly vertical and axisymmetric for 4-6 minutes, although each dossier documents drift or shear (Grable: violent NE shear; Trinity: NE dust sheet and NW cap; Little Boy: NW drift). Add a per-bomb wind profile that offsets head and stem with height and time.

SCENE CONTEXT IN THE ZOOM VIEW: the foreground terrain is a smooth gradient with long horizontal streak bands near the horizon (terrain LOD or grazing-angle texture aliasing). No range objects, destruction, heat haze or cloud shadow are readable, and Baker shows desert sand instead of a lagoon. Per-bomb environments (dawn for Trinity, water for Baker) must be part of the canonical review render, or the signatures cannot be judged.

COLOUR PIPELINE (severity 3, all four bombs): volume albedo barely affects the final colour. B83's dark brown stem [0.24,0.18,0.13] renders (161,170,180), the same as Ivy King's light stem [0.72,0.70,0.68] at (163,172,181), and Sedan's dark dust column renders white. Distant volumes are much BRIGHTER than the horizon sky behind them (horizon ~(110,126,136) vs volumes 150-192). Cause: the aerial-perspective in-scatter colour (environment_ctl NOON fog_col 0.50/0.58/0.70 * fog_bright 0.85 + sun term) is brighter than the sky shader's horizon radiance. The fog amount at 35-60 km is also 0.55-0.7 (sigma 1.8e-5 near the ground + 5e-6 Rayleigh), and the volume adds a strong blue ambient term (amb*ao*0.6 with amb 0.30/0.38/0.52). Fix: derive g_fog_color from the sky model's horizon radiance in the view azimuth (or calibrate fog_bright ~0.45 so a 200 km path equals the horizon sky). Lower noon desert haze to ~0.8-1.0e-5 (Nevada visibility 200+ km). In explosion_volume, cut the ambient to ~0.3 and tint it toward ground bounce for dust. Increase sun/shade contrast (macro = dot*0.75+0.25). Then re-verify that NOx red-brown, dark dirt stems and tan surges read as such.

CAP LATERAL GROWTH (severity 3, Ivy King/B83/RDS-37, and probably every NUCLEAR_* bomb): explosion_profile.head_state grows the radius with 1-(1-min(1.25*tanh(t/tau),1))^1.6. This reaches ~25% of the final 10-min cap radius by 20 s and ~80% by 90 s. Result: 13-16 km wide pancakes at 40 s (measured King: 3.4 km at 60 s) and a visible pop from a 1-2 km fireball to a 5-8 km ellipsoid between 5 s and 20 s. Fix: power-law growth from breakaway, r = lerp(start_r, cap_r, pow(clamp((t - t_fb_max)/(1.2-1.3*t_stab), 0, 1), 0.9)), with an optional per-bomb cap_d60_m calibration.

BUNKER EMBRASURE CLIPS THE CLIMAX (severity 3): in the zoom/binocular view the bunker roof covers everything above ~13 deg elevation. The 20-23 km clouds of Ivy King (24.7 deg), B83 (20.9 deg) and RDS-37 (18.4 deg) are cut off from ~90 s, and the 180-360 s frames show only stems through the slit. The same will hit Mike/Bravo/219/Tsar. Fix: binocular camera on the roof/berm parapet, or cull the bunker layer when zoomed, plus a taller embrasure/periscope for gameplay.

EARTH CURVATURE vs RECOMMENDED DISTANCE (severity 2-3): with R_eff 8.5e6 the hidden height is ~72 m at 35 km, 147 m at 50 km, 178 m at 55 km and 212 m at 60 km. This erases ground-level signatures: the entire Sedan dome and vent; the B83 hemisphere base, crater and stem foot; the RDS-37/King dust skirts and Mach ring. Choose rec_km per bomb so the key ground feature is above the horizon (Sedan ~8-10 km, B83 ~30 km), or raise the observer eye on the berm. Also make shot_rig zoom framing account for dome_state/stem, not only head and fireball.

SIGNATURE DISTINCTNESS (severity 3, task 6.3): bombs 14, 15 and 16 produce the same sequence (clipped white ball -> grey banded igloo -> pink marshmallow pancake -> white stem with a Saturn ring). The per-bomb profile differences (colours, stem density) are swamped by the shared lighting, growth and condensation code. After the pipeline fixes, give each bomb a distinct silhouette and palette, and verify with side-by-side sheets at the same ages.

FIREBALL IN ZOOM (severity 2): from 0.1 s to 5-10 s every megaton ball is a fully clipped flat white disc with an oversized bloom. There is no limb darkening, no rapatronic mottling and no visible second-peak structure, which fails the 6.4 'not plasticine' check, and white 'firefly' sparkles float at the limb (tiny noise blobs at HDR emission). Fix: binocular metering headroom (max_comp up to ~13-14 stops when the ball fills the view), stronger limb darkening, emission gated by density (smoothstep(0.3,0.8,df)) plus a per-sample HDR clamp, and less glow during the flash in zoom.

CONDENSATION PRIMITIVES LOOK CG (severity 2): rings are detached constant-thickness tori with a gap to the stem; ice_cap is a ghost outline lasting 0.45*t_stab; tier2 is a flat speckled saucer. The Wilson shell (in these renders) is an opaque grey 32-ring SphereMesh with latitude banding. Fixes: rings hug the stem as thin noisy collars; pileus lives ~20-40 s and hugs the dome; tier2 becomes an open bell; Wilson uses a high-res mesh or the volume SDF, stays thin, bright and fireball-lit with alpha <= 0.4. Note: the post-render change that disables Wilson for >150 kt also deletes documented features (King and RDS-37 condensation domes/discs); use wilson_force with a proper look instead.

RAYMARCH ARTIFACTS (severity 2): hard planar seams where the stem's flat sdf_stem top cuts inside the head (Sedan 5 s; RDS-37 'tin can' stem), hard-edged cut-out holes from the dens<0.04 -> 0 threshold, horizontal streak banding in stems, grainy dither speckle in thin shells, and crisp analytic shadow lines from the noise-free cheap_density. Fix: smooth the top fade on stems, a soft density threshold, blue-noise per-pixel dither, dt capped relative to the local structure size, higher base_steps for the offline/movie render, and softened/noised shadow density.

NO TORUS OR CAULIFLOWER (severity 2): caps are smooth ellipsoids with uniform fine 'cotton wool' noise, flat undersides, no visible roll/torus and weak self-shadowing. Increase large-scale billow amplitude (head_noise_amp ~0.45-0.55, larger cells), keep torus visible with roll, add darker undersides and stronger sun/shade contrast.

EXPOSURE (severity 2): after megaton flashes the sky stays black until 20-40 s although 90% of the thermal energy is emitted by 8-11 s. Buried shots (Sedan) trigger a ~0.5-stop dip from an invisible vent glow. Meter only on the visible fireball emission and shorten the recovery once the target drops.

TERRAIN/SKY IN ZOOM (severity 1): the narrow-FOV view shows the desert as flat horizontal painted stripes (texture stretched at grazing angles, no micro-detail or scrub). The noon sky is a dull grey-teal rather than the deep desert blue of the Sedan colour reference.

NOTE: the r2 renders (07:18-07:19) predate edits to explosion_profile.gd (07:19), fx_layers.gd (07:22), explosion.gd (07:23) and the shaders (07:36). Some items (e.g. the Wilson igloo on megaton shots) may already be changed. Re-render bombs 13-16 before the next review cycle.

These renders are out of date. They were made at 07:19, but explosion.gd, explosion_profile.gd, fx_layers.gd, wilson.gdshader, explosion_volume.gdshader and shot_rig.gd were all changed between 07:19 and 07:32. The b19 and b20 logs also show parse errors in range_objects.gd (_ico_v and _ico_f not declared), so those two renders were made without range objects. Re-render all four after the fixes. The grey domes at 10-58 s match the WilsonLayer timing exactly (t0 = (W/20)^(1/3), lasting to t0 + 2.2*1.5*t0); the new w_kt>150 rule should remove them, so confirm it.

Zoom framing fails for every megaton after about 90 s. The bunker ceiling beam and roof cover the top 30-50% of the frame, and Bravo falls back to the 58 deg clamp, which shows the window frame and consoles. The caps, anvils, two-tier caps and overshooting tops are never seen. In binocular or zoom mode, exclude the bunker-interior layer from the camera's cull_mask (or put the eye at the embrasure's outer face) and allow pitch up to ~30 deg.

Cap lateral growth is front-loaded in ExplosionProfile.head_state. It uses grow = 1-(1-1.25*tanh(t/tau))^1.6, which gives 30-40% of the final cap radius by 40 s. All four caps come out 3-5x too wide in the first 1-2 minutes: flat 4:1 pancakes with stubby stems instead of rising cauliflower balls. Data-drive height and diameter from the dossier with top_keys and cap_d_keys (log-time interpolation). At minimum, spread the radius roughly linearly in time (cap_r*t/(0.9*t_stab)).

Fireball colour is lost to exposure and AgX. Every fireball is clipped pure white from 0.1 s to 20-40 s; there is no white -> yellow -> orange -> red progression, no thermal-minimum dip and no rapatronic mottling. Fix metered_luminance to spot-weight the fireball, aiming for about +1.5 EV rather than +3-4 EV. Add a per-bomb late-cooling factor, because fireball_temperature is still 2500-3500 K at 40 s for megatons. Use the megaton t_min and t2 scaling, 0.0025*W^0.5 and 0.032*W^0.5, or per-bomb overrides.

The fireball and the cloud head are separate primitives. A hard-edged hot sphere floats inside or in front of a pale cap with separate glow lobes ('face', 'Saturn', 'lamp in a bell jar'). The head must grow out of the fireball (start_r = fireball radius, same centre) while fireball opacity cross-fades into head_heat.

Fireball light on nearby media is far too weak. In explosion_volume.gdshader the term is light += blackbody*fl*0.03*..., and the Wilson and dust shaders use about 0.02*g_fireball_color. Clouds and shells next to a sun-bright ball therefore stay matte grey. Use a physically scaled inverse-square term (albedo * L_fb * (R/d)^2, a factor of ~0.5-1 instead of 0.03), so caps, pileus, rings and skirts glow yellow-orange as in every reference photo.

The four megatons are near-identical scaled copies: the same white ball, grey dome, pancake cap, fluffy brim, donut rings, white stem and white skirt slab. This violates section 6.3. Each needs its own lighting and time of day: Mike at sunrise with a cumulus deck, Bravo pre-dawn and crimson, 219 polar night silhouette, Tsar at low arctic sun with an overcast hole. Each also needs its own features: Mike's water curtain and dirty red-brown stem, Bravo's thin stacked discs and bells, 219 and Tsar with flat-bottomed fireballs, no Wilson and no rings, and Tsar's two-tier cap.

Condensation rings are drawn as thick hollow tori. sdf_rings uses radial factor 0.35 and thickness 0.12*rr, giving 1.5-2 km thick bands with a sky hole and a specular hot spot. Their timing is also off: they appear at 0.05*t_stab and live 0.36*t_stab, so they are absent at 30-60 s and present at 3-5 min. Make them flat laminar discs 100-300 m thick with per-bomb times and heights.

Aerial perspective washes out explosion albedo at 90-150 km (col = mix(acc, fog, fog.a) in the volume shader). Dark stems (Bravo 0.30) and dusty skirts render the same pale blue-white as the horizon haze. Scale fog.a for the volume by about 0.4-0.5, or derive it from a realistic visibility of 150-250 km.

The raymarch is too coarse when the proxy box grows to 60-110 km (tier2 and rings enlarge it). With base_steps 64, steps are about 1 km, which produces stacked, banded 'screw' and pagoda patterns and helical facets in stems at 180-360 s. March per-component intervals, or clamp dt near small structures (dt <= 0.05*stem radius), and raise steps to 128-192 for cine and megatons.

Head noise scales with max(R,H)*0.55, and the edge softness is H*0.03. On 30-50 km caps the finest billows are about 5 km and the edges blur by about 1 km, giving an out-of-focus cotton look with weak self-shadowing. Base the noise cell on H or an absolute scale, add an octave, sharpen the edges and strengthen micro self-shadow so the crevices go dark.

There are hard CG shapes. The skirt is a flat slab with a vertical outer wall (the sheet term in sdf_skirt). The stem has a flat cut top during growth (max(d,dv)). The stem's sun terminator is hard, which reads as a twisted rope. The ice-cap shell sits at y = top - 0.25r and becomes a fluffy brim at mid-height. Soften all of these.
The fireball remnant persists too long. Fireball opacity only fades below 2150 K, so orange specks remain inside the cap underside at 90-180 s. Fade opacity on a time basis (t_fb_max to 3*t_fb_max).
The shock-shell refraction rim draws hairline circles over the fireball (0.5-1 s) and across the cloud and sky at 40-90 s. Hide it inside 1.3x the fireball radius and fade it below about 1 psi.

Surface bursts (Mike, Bravo) float. fireball_state places the centre at 0.46*r_fb_max above the ground from t=0 because head_center_y(0) = r_fb_max*0.5. They should be flat-based hemispheres that hug the ground until lift-off at ~10 s.

The initial flash or white-out is not in the captured frames: the 2-20 ms frames look like a hazy sunny day. The white-out is only a UI overlay (ui.flash_white). Move it into the world (sky g_flash, terrain and bloom) so movie-mode renders get the blinding first frames.
